name: Packshot Studio
description: One phone photo of a garment in, a full catalogue set out: front, back and flat-lay packshots plus collar, cuff, fabric and button close-ups — all on white in one light, the garment's true colour and fabric kept from your photo.
markdownDescription:
## Packshot Studio

One phone photo of a garment — on a bed, in bad light — becomes a full catalogue set: three packshots and four detail close-ups, all on white in one light. No studio, no mannequin, no example photos to hunt for.

1. **Phone photo** — the garment as it is, however it was shot. Every image gets it as the reference for colour and fabric.
2. **Light + Shop style** — the studio light from tiles and one line about your background and shadow.
3. **Garment notes** — an AI reads the phone photo once and writes the garment down: fabric, true colour, collar, buttons, seams.
4. **Row 1, the packshots** — front, back, flat lay. The shop page.
5. **Row 2, the details** — collar, cuff, fabric, button. The zoom.
6. Swap the phone photo and rerun everything; change the shop-style line and every image follows.

Garment notes
data.userInput: Describe the garment in the reference photo. Correct for the colour cast of the light.
data.systemPrompt: You write garment descriptions for an image generator from an amateur phone photo. Ignore the surroundings, the crooked framing and the colour cast of the lamp; describe the garment as it truly is in ONE paragraph of 50–70 words, plain declarative English: garment type, fabric and knit or weave, true colour, collar, closure and buttons (material, count), pockets, cuffs, hem, fit and proportions. Only what is visible. No brand names, no opinions, no bullet points, no commentary. Output only the paragraph.
